author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Zscaler Private Access User Activity and User Status logs, which LSS streams through an App Connector to the data collector's TCP listener. User Activity records go to Netflow and User Status records to Auth; other LSS log types stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- Add a ZPA log receiver for the data collector's TCP listener and pick the JSON template for the User Activity and User Status log types; LSS streams them through an App Connector.
- The parser reads the default JSON templates by key name, so keep the key names; a syslog header added by a relay is fine.

Field mapping:
- User Activity records go to Netflow and User Status records to Auth.
- App Connector, Service Edge, audit and other LSS log types stay generic.
- Netflow has no user field, so the user name, session and connection IDs, policy and App Connector go to event_metadata.
- flow_action is FW_BLOCKED for Zscaler's policy block status codes, FW_ALLOWED for open connections and normal closes, and unset for connection errors such as APP_NOT_REACHABLE.
- Byte counts are running totals for the connection, so take volumes from the close record.

Time:
- LogTimestamp is read as UTC, in its default ctime form or as ISO 8601.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the default templates' key order.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser in that tenant matched these lines.

Known gaps:
- LSS can resend the last 15 minutes after an outage, so expect some duplicates.
